title: Learning Better Certified Models from Empirically-Robust Teachers
claim: Increasing the distillation strength leaves standard and adversarial accuracy stable but shifts certified accuracy, with a chosen intermediate value working well.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend in right panel, dashed vertical marker
description: Two side-by-side line plots show accuracy in percent against distillation coefficient βw on a log-like x-axis that starts at 0. The left panel is for ε=2/255 and the right for ε=8/255. Four dotted, marker-coded series appear in both: Standard (blue triangles), Adversarial (orange inverted triangles), BaB-certified (green squares) and CROWN/IBP-certified (red diamonds). In the left panel the series are well separated: standard is about 80–82, adversarial about 69–71, BaB about 63–65 and CROWN/IBP about 47–53. In the right panel standard is near 55 and the other three cluster tightly at about 33–37. A green dashed vertical line marks the β value used in the paper. The legend sits inside the right plot. Captions (a) and (b) give ε below each panel.
caption: \looseness=-1 Standard, empirical adversarial and certified accuracies (BaB and CROWN/IBP) under $\ell_\infty$ perturbations of networks trained using CC-Dist under varying distillation coefficient $\beta$. The legend is reported once for all subfigures in plot [ref]. Metrics are reported on the CIFAR-10 test set. The $\beta$ value employed throughout the paper (see $\S$[ref]) is marked by a dashed vertical line.
abstract: Adversarial training attains strong empirical robustness to specific adversarial attacks by training on concrete adversarial perturbations, but it produces neural networks that are not amenable to strong robustness certificates through neural network verification. On the other hand, earlier certified training schemes directly train on bounds from network relaxations to obtain models that are certifiably robust, but display sub-par standard performance. Recent work has shown that state-of-the-art trade-offs between certified robustness and standard performance can be obtained through a family of losses combining adversarial outputs and neural network bounds. Nevertheless, differently from empirical robustness, verifiability still comes at a significant cost in standard performance. In this work, we propose to leverage empirically-robust teachers to improve the performance of certifiably-robust models through knowledge distillation. Using versatile feature-space distillation objectives, we show that distillation from adversarially-trained teachers can significantly improve the performance of state-of-the-art certified training algorithms for ReLU networks on robust computer vision benchmarks.
